title: The plain meeting house
hookLine: Quaker and Puritan rooms of white walls and clear glass

cards: White walls. Clear glass. Wooden benches.
No statues, no painted windows, no altar. In a Quaker meeting house the benches may face each other, with no pulpit at all. People come in, sit down, and the room goes quiet.
A clock ticks. Outside, a branch moves. After a while, someone stands, says a few sentences, and sits down.

In an old New England meeting house built by Puritans, the room is just as bare, but everything turns toward a high pulpit where the Bible is read and preached. Two plain rooms, built that way on purpose.

teach.h: DWELLETH NOT IN TEMPLES MADE WITH HANDS.
teach.b: Yesterday's cathedral asked how a building can lift the eye toward God. The meeting house, from the same Bible, asks what might stand in the way. Start with the building.
In Athens, Paul tells a crowd standing among temples: "God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands."
Plain builders leaned hard on that line. The room shelters the people, and that's its job. Next, the worship.
Jesus tells a Samaritan woman at a well, "God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth."
Puritans wanted worship stripped back to what they found in scripture, so the Bible, read and preached, stands at the center. Quakers went another way into the same plainness.

As day two hundred seventy-nine told, they speak of the light of Christ within each person, and they hear it in John's Gospel: "That was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world."
So in a Quaker meeting of the silent kind, anyone may rise and speak, and no one has to.

teach.h: WHERE TWO OR THREE ARE GATHERED.
teach.b: Then, the people: "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them." In this reading, the gathering is the room's holy center. Last, the clear glass.
No saints in the window, just the real sky and the real tree. On the mountain, Elijah learns that the LORD was not in the wind, the earthquake or the fire.

teach.h: CLEAR GLASS: A STILL SMALL VOICE.
teach.b: After the fire came "a still small voice."

how: In unprogrammed Quaker meetings, people gather in a plain room and sit in silence, and anyone may rise to speak when moved; churches in the Puritan and Reformed line gather in plain rooms centered on the reading and preaching of the Bible.

games.q: what does “the plain meeting house” mean?
o: a hall where a church holds business meetings
a bare room for worship, with nothing in the way
a simple chapel for weddings and funerals

games.q: the plain room — tap the pairs.
p: dwelleth not in temples made with hands
Jesus, to a woman at a well
John's Gospel, a line Quakers hear

s: a plain meeting house means its builders didn't care about worship
it's plain on purpose: they wanted nothing to stand between the gathered people and God.
in a silent Quaker meeting, anyone may stand and speak
someone rises when moved, says a few sentences, and sits; then the quiet returns.
a Quaker meeting can't begin until a minister leads it
in the silent kind of meeting, people simply gather, sit, and wait together.

games.q: you're in a silent Quaker meeting. a long quiet, and one thought keeps coming back to you. what happens next?
o: wait for the minister to call on you
stand, say it plainly, and sit down again
write it on a card for later
games.why: anyone may rise and speak when moved, briefly. then they sit, and the silence comes back.

practice: Find the barest spot you can, a blank wall or an empty table, and sit with nothing to look at and nothing to do, letting thoughts pass.
If you pray, wait the way a Quaker meeting waits, without asking for anything, listening for a still small voice. If you don't, sit in the quiet and let the plainness be enough.

wordCard.voice: The plain meeting house. A room kept bare on purpose, so that nothing stands between the gathered people and God.

orig.note: Hebrew: the "still small voice" Elijah meets after the wind, earthquake and fire (1 Kings 19:12).

carryVoice: Your line: nothing between. Just the gathered people, the quiet, and the real sky. Until tomorrow.
